 NorthEast United seek sixth unbeaten game as FC Goa visit 
 By
 TNM NewsDesk 
 ✓
 20 November 2026, 4:01 pm 
 3 min read
 20 Nov 2026 
 Redeem Tlang of NorthEast United FC 
 NorthEast United FC will look to extend their unbeaten start to six matches when they host FC Goa at the Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati on November 21, 2026, as the Indian Super League resumes after the international break.
 The match kicks off at 7.30 pm IST and will be Ángel Viadero’s first as FC Goa head coach. Previously an assistant to NorthEast United coach Juan Pedro Benali, Viadero will face a friend of 25 years in the opposing dugout.

 “Ángel is my brother but during the game, there are no brothers. He’s my opponent,” Benali said on the eve of the fixture. “On the pitch, I wouldn’t even recognise my own father! But off it, we give each other a hug. Before and after the game, we’re brothers.”
 NorthEast United have 11 points from five matches. They beat Mohun Bagan Super Giant through Jithin’s stoppage-time winner, scored four goals against Kerala Blasters and drew with Odisha FC and Bengaluru FC before defeating Churchill Brothers in Fatorda.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Ethyan González and Antonio Moyano scored in that latest victory, with Moyano adding the second in stoppage time. Jithin, Alaaeddine Ajaraie and Moyano have scored twice apiece this season. Goalkeeper Gurmeet Singh has kept three clean sheets, while the team have conceded only two goals.
 “A break interrupts your rhythm, and getting it back takes time. But I trust my players,” Benali said.
 During the international break, NorthEast United technical director Naushad Moosa led India to the SAFF Championship 2026 title as head coach.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Defender Eneko Satrústegui attributed NorthEast United’s defensive understanding to the players’ growing familiarity with one another.
 “We’ve played quite a few games together now. We know each other a little better, and we know how to help each other,” he said.
 On his first season with the club, he added: “I feel like a child. I want to play more and more games, but we’ll take it step by step.”
 FC Goa have five points from four matches. After opening with two draws, they won 2-1 at Inter Kashi before losing by the same score to Bengaluru FC, who struck the winner in stoppage time.
 Francisco Feuillassier scored in both games. Muhammed Nemil set up Christian Borrego’s winner against Inter Kashi and supplied the equaliser against Bengaluru.
 Of the teams’ 23 previous ISL meetings, 12 have ended in draws. Goa have won seven and NorthEast United four. NorthEast United won their Super Cup encounter 2-1 last November, while Goa won 2-0 in Guwahati in the league in April.
 Benali said his familiarity with Viadero would not remove the need to adapt during the match.
 “We’ll need to read the game in the first ten minutes. Whatever you prepare for, there’s always something different,” he said.
